newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent basis listless as NYMEX spikes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent basis listless as NYMEX spikes.

text.p: Refined product prices may be spiking sharply Tuesday in line with pre-expiry volatility, but cash differentials were dead in the water in midday talk, with traders largely watching the screen, traders said.
"It's a technical move and the (spot) market looks bored. Values are pretty much where they were yesterday," said one midcontinent trader.

Some players were also waiting for this week's stocks data from the American Petroleum Institute (API), which, according to a Reuter survey, should show gasoline and distillate stocks fell last week by 500,000 and one million barrels.
Low sulphur diesel remained 7.25/7.50 cents a gallon over NYMEX May heating oil in Group Three and 1.25/1.50 cents over the print in Chicago, traders said.
High sulphur also was unchanged at 6.75/7.0 cents over the print in Group Three and 0.75/1.0 cents over the print in Chicago, traders said.
Unleaded gasoline differentials opened the week unchanged at bids 1.50 cents a gallon under NYMEX May unleaded in Group Three and 1.0 cent under the print in Chicago, traders said.
-- Oliver Ludwig New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
